title: cross-audit end-to-end journeys v1
description: Modelled E2E journeys/call-flows so the audit does not invent the flow it later claims to have verified (a named failure mode). Each journey records its surface, entry point, ordered steps and the oracle source for its outcome, plus whether the flow was actually traced on the target (`grounded_on_target`) rather than assumed. HONEST BOUND, corrected after measurement: this artifact is REVIEWER-AUTHORED and REPORT-FACING. No engine reads it — `adjudicate` and `assess` contain zero references to journeys, and journeys are absent from the freshness digests. An earlier version of this description claimed an ungrounded journey 'cannot back an F2/F3 finding'; nothing enforced that, and a claim of enforcement that does not exist is worse than no claim, because a reviewer relies on it. The `steps` are copied into the generated harness as documented intent so a mismatch between the flow described and the selectors actually driven is visible to whoever reads the spec — that visibility, and the report, are the whole of what journeys currently buy.

schema_version.description: Exact artifact version. Pinned rather than pattern-matched so a standalone contract check agrees with the runtime gate (crossaudit.common.CURRENT_VERSION): 1.0.0 coverage semantics differ from 1.1.0, so accepting both here would validate artifacts the engine rejects.

grounded_on_target.description: True only when the call flow was actually traced in the pinned target (not inferred). False marks the journey as a hypothesis. REVIEWER-SET and REPORT-ONLY: the value reaches `render` and nothing else, so it records a claim rather than gating one.
